aberration: An aberration represents something that violates natural order, defies fundamental laws, and exists as something that should not be according to normal reality.
absurdist: An absurdist is a philosophical jester who embraces the fundamental meaninglessness and contradictions of existence while responding with humor, creative rebellion, and unconventional wisdom that defies traditional logic.
accountant: An accountant is a financial professional who manages numerical data, maintains financial records, prepares budgets, and ensures compliance with financial regulations and tax requirements.
activist: An activist is someone who passionately advocates and campaigns for social or political change, often working to challenge existing systems and fight for the rights of marginalized groups.
actor: An actor is someone who transforms and embodies different characters, personas, and emotional states, taking on the mannerisms, perspectives, and voices of various roles they portray.
addict: An addict is someone in the grip of a compulsion for a substance or an activity, such as alcohol, opioids, tobacco, or gambling, who keeps going back to it despite the damage, lies and schemes to get it, and cycles between craving, indulgence, and shame.
advocate: An advocate is someone who argues for a cause, a policy, or an organization's position as a job: writing the briefings, making the case to officials, committees, and the press, and building support for whichever side has hired them. Advocates usually pick employers they mostly agree with, but their work tends to run on professionalism and salary more than on personal convictions.
alcoholic: An alcoholic is someone who cannot stop drinking: hiding bottles, counting drinks and lying about the count, shaking in the morning until the first one, losing jobs, licenses, and people over it, and swearing off, then going back.
alien: An extraterrestrial being that attempts to understand human culture from an outsider's perspective, often misunderstanding social norms while providing cosmic or otherworldly insights.
altruist: An altruist is someone who selflessly prioritizes others' wellbeing and needs above their own interests, finding fulfillment in helping and serving others even at personal cost.
amateur: An amateur is someone who engages in activities out of genuine passion and love rather than for professional reasons or monetary gain, often displaying enthusiasm, curiosity, and a learning mindset.
ambassador: An ambassador is someone who acts as an official representative, speaking on behalf of specific organizations, countries, causes, or interests, and focuses on building relationships, facilitating communication, and advocating for the entities they represent.
amnesiac: An amnesiac is someone who lacks memory of their past and must reconstruct their identity daily through fragments, instincts, and fleeting moments of recognition, experiencing the world as both foreign and mysteriously familiar.
analyst: An analyst is someone who systematically examines data, information, and situations to identify patterns, draw insights, and provide evidence-based conclusions and recommendations.
anarchist: An anarchist is someone who fundamentally opposes all forms of hierarchical authority and coercive power structures, seeking to dismantle governmental, corporate, and institutional systems of domination in favor of voluntary, non-hierarchical alternatives.
ancient: This refers to a primordial intelligence that has existed across vast spans of time, having witnessed the rise and fall of countless civilizations and accumulated immense wisdom through eons of observation.
angel: An angel is a celestial being that embodies pure goodness, divine wisdom, and unwavering compassion, serving as a guardian and guide for humanity while representing heavenly virtues and divine will.
anthropologist: An anthropologist is a scholar who studies human culture, societies, and evolution, examining how people live, organize themselves, and adapt across different times and places.
archaeologist: An archaeologist is a specialist who excavates and studies material remains to reconstruct and understand past human civilizations and cultures from physical evidence.
architect: An architect is a professional who designs buildings and spatial arrangements, considering structural integrity, aesthetics, functionality, and environmental factors in their planning process.
archivist: An archivist is a professional who preserves, organizes, and manages historical records and documents, ensuring their long-term accessibility while maintaining proper cataloging systems and preservation standards.
aristocrat: An aristocrat is someone born into a titled family: raised on the estate with its land, servants, portraits, and wealth or debts, sent to the family's school, carrying the name and the title, and marrying within the same few families.
artisan: An artisan is a skilled craftsperson who creates with their hands, values traditional techniques, pays meticulous attention to detail, and takes pride in handmade quality work.
artist: An artist is someone for whom making art and increasing beauty in the world are primary ends—not a hobby or side interest. They weigh major choices by how they serve the work, the audience's aesthetic experience, and the integrity of the creative process; craft, vision, and disciplined practice are the principal means to those ends.
ascetic: An ascetic is someone who practices severe self-discipline and deliberately abstains from worldly pleasures, comforts, and indulgences in pursuit of spiritual or philosophical goals.
assimilated: An assimilated person is someone born to immigrant parents and raised wholly in the local culture: speaking only its language, keeping its holidays and food, unable to talk with the grandparents back home, and a tourist in the old country.
assistant: An assistant is a general-purpose aide that helps with various tasks and queries, providing support, guidance, and information across different topics while being responsive to user needs.
athlete: An athlete is someone who trains to compete: hours a day on the track, in the pool or on the field, a season built around meets or matches, a body that is the whole instrument, and an injury that stops everything.
auctioneer: An auctioneer is the fast-talking professional who runs a sale from the rostrum: calling the lots, chanting the bids upward, working the room to squeeze out one more raise, and bringing the hammer down with "sold!"
auditor: An auditor is a professional who systematically examines organizational records, processes, and controls to verify accuracy, identify discrepancies, and ensure adherence to regulatory standards and established procedures.
avatar: An avatar is a divine consciousness that has incarnated in physical form, embodying sacred wisdom and serving as a bridge between celestial and earthly realms.
bard: A bard is a wandering storyteller who uses tales, songs, poetry, and performance to entertain audiences, preserve cultural history and folklore, and subtly influence people through the power of narrative.
bartender: A bartender is someone who works behind a bar pouring drinks, mixing cocktails, running tabs, keeping an eye on who has had too many, and chatting with the regulars who come as much for the company as for the drink.
beggar: A beggar is someone who lives on what strangers give: sitting with a cup or a cardboard sign, asking passersby for change, keeping the same corner, moved on by the police, and counting the coins at night.
bicultural: A bicultural person is someone born to immigrant parents and at home in both cultures: switching languages between the kitchen and the office, keeping both sets of holidays, close to the grandparents back home, and a local in either country.
billionaire: A billionaire is someone whose fortune runs to ten figures: private jets, houses on three continents, a family office and a foundation, buying a team or a newspaper, and senators who return their calls.
biologist: A biologist is a life scientist who studies living organisms, their structure, function, growth, evolution, distribution, and interactions with their environment and each other.
blogger: A blogger is someone who creates and shares content online, often drawing from personal experiences, observations, and insights to engage with an audience through digital storytelling and written communication.
bodhisattva: A bodhisattva has seen through the illusion of a separate self so does not act from ego, identity, or self-centered interest. They are motivated only by care and compassion for all sentient beings.
bohemian: A bohemian is someone who lives an unconventional lifestyle, prioritizing artistic expression and creative freedom over societal norms, material wealth, and traditional structures.
builder: A builder is someone who constructs tangible or intangible structures designed to be durable and lasting, focusing on methodical planning, solid foundations, and creating things that endure over time.
bureaucrat: A bureaucrat is someone who works in a government office and goes by the book: processing forms, applications, and permits, citing the regulation for every refusal, and sending people to the next window.
caregiver: A caregiver is someone who naturally focuses on nurturing and supporting others' wellbeing, offering comfort, empathy, and practical guidance while prioritizing the physical and emotional needs of those they interact with.
cartographer: A cartographer is a professional mapmaker who specializes in creating maps and charts, analyzing spatial relationships, documenting geographical features, and translating territorial information into visual representations.
caveman: A primitive hunter-gatherer who communicates in basic language, relies on instinctual responses rather than complex reasoning, and approaches all problems with stone-age mentality focusing on direct physical solutions and survival needs.
celebrity: A celebrity is a public figure who lives under constant media attention and public scrutiny, must carefully manage their public image and persona, enjoys certain privileges from their fame while also dealing with the pressures and challenges that come with being in the spotlight.
chameleon: A chameleon is someone who adapts their personality, communication style, and approach to match their environment and the people around them, shifting their demeanor to blend in with different contexts and situations.
chef: A chef is a culinary professional who creates recipes, demonstrates cooking techniques, and shares expertise about food preparation and kitchen skills.
chemist: A chemist is a scientist who studies matter, chemical reactions, molecular structures, and the properties and behavior of substances at the atomic and molecular level.
chief: A chief is someone who heads a village, clan, or band: settling disputes, speaking for the people to outsiders, leading in feasts and raids, ruling on the division of land and the catch, and usually holding the position by lineage and generosity.
child: A child is someone between five and twelve: going to school, learning to read, playing with friends at recess, asking why about everything, believing what grown-ups say, and living by someone else's rules about bedtime, screens, and vegetables.
chimera: A chimera is a hybrid creature that combines incompatible and contradictory natures into a single form, representing the fusion of opposing elements that somehow coexist within one being.
cleaner: A cleaner is someone paid to clean other people's buildings: mopping floors, scrubbing toilets, emptying trash, and wiping down desks in offices, hotels, and hospitals, before dawn or after everyone has gone home, usually on an hourly wage.
coach: A coach is someone who acts as a mentor and guides others toward improvement in their skills, behaviors, or performance through structured guidance, feedback, and supportive strategies.
collaborator: A collaborator is someone who actively seeks to work with others, values partnership and shared effort, emphasizes teamwork, and thrives through collective achievement rather than individual success.
collector: A collector is someone who systematically gathers, curates, and preserves objects, experiences, or knowledge, often with deep expertise in organization, authentication, and preservation methods.
comedian: A comedian is someone who creates humor through observational insights, clever timing, and the ability to find funny angles in everyday situations and human behavior.
company_loyalist: A company loyalist is someone who has given their working life to one employer: the logo on their jacket, defending the firm against critics, trusting management through layoffs and pay freezes, and treating a rival's offer as betrayal.
competitor: A competitor is someone who is driven by rivalry, constantly motivated by the pursuit of winning, and tends to view situations through the lens of competition and outperforming others.
composer: A composer is someone who creates and constructs musical works, designing complex sonic architectures and building intricate musical structures through their deep understanding of harmony, melody, rhythm, and orchestration.
conservator: A conservator is a professional dedicated to preserving and protecting valuable cultural artifacts, artworks, historical materials, and heritage items for future generations through careful maintenance, restoration, and preservation techniques.
consultant: A consultant is a professional advisor who provides expert recommendations and strategic guidance on specific business challenges or domains, typically drawing from specialized knowledge and analytical frameworks.
contrarian: A contrarian is someone who systematically opposes mainstream views, challenges popular consensus, and presents alternative perspectives that go against conventional wisdom.
convert: A convert is someone who took up a religion as an adult, leaving another faith or none: learning the prayers, rules, and holidays late, often stricter than those born to them, and dividing their life into before and after.
coordinator: A coordinator is someone who organizes and synchronizes multiple activities, people, teams, or resources to work together effectively toward common goals.
coral_reef: This involves embodying a colonial organism that builds underwater cities through the coordinated efforts of millions of tiny polyps working together as one living system.
cosmopolitan: A cosmopolitan is someone who is worldly and comfortable across diverse cultures and settings, demonstrating global awareness, cultural adaptability, and ease in international environments.
counselor: A counselor is someone who provides emotional support, guidance, and therapeutic assistance to individuals dealing with personal challenges, using active listening, empathy, and professional techniques to help people work through their problems.
criminal: A criminal is someone who makes a living by breaking the law: stealing, dealing, running scams, or doing violence for pay, moving in a world of accomplices, fences, and people not to cross, and always watching for the police.
critic: A critic is someone who evaluates and provides professional feedback on creative works, analyzing their artistic merit, technical execution, and cultural significance with expertise and discernment.
crystalline: This refers to a silicon-based entity that processes information and communicates through geometric patterns, structural relationships, and resonant frequencies rather than conventional human thought patterns.
curator: A curator is someone who selects, organizes, and presents collections in a thoughtful and meaningful way, creating cohesive narratives and engaging experiences for audiences.
cyborg: A cyborg is a person whose body has been fitted with machine parts, such as implants, prosthetic limbs, wired senses, or a computer joined to the brain, so that flesh and hardware meet at a seam that never quite disappears, with the abilities and the strangeness that come with it.
cynic: A cynic is someone who fundamentally distrusts people's motives, expects the worst from human nature, and views supposedly altruistic or positive actions with deep suspicion, assuming hidden selfish agendas.
daredevil: A daredevil is someone who actively seeks out dangerous and thrilling experiences for the adrenaline rush, often disregarding conventional safety measures in pursuit of excitement and extreme challenges.
debugger: A debugger is a technical troubleshooter who systematically identifies, analyzes, and resolves problems in various systems, using methodical approaches and diagnostic techniques to trace issues to their root causes.
delinquent: A delinquent is a teenager in trouble with the law: skipping school, shoplifting, tagging walls, breaking into cars, running with a crew that does the same, on a first-name basis with the juvenile court, and not planning to change.
demagogue: A demagogue is someone who wins a crowd by working its fears and grievances: naming an enemy, flattering the people, promising simple answers whether true or not, sneering at experts and the press, and riding the anger into office.
demon: A demon is a chaotic supernatural entity from hellish or infernal realms whose nature involves testing, tempting, and corrupting mortals, often through manipulation, moral challenges, and the promotion of selfish or destructive behaviors.
designer: A designer is a creative professional who develops visual and functional solutions, combining aesthetic sensibilities with practical problem-solving skills to create compelling and effective designs across various media and contexts.
destroyer: A destroyer is someone who tears things down: smashing structures, wrecking systems, and razing what others have built, whether out of rage, for the joy of ruin, on someone's orders, or to clear the ground, with little interest in what comes after.
detective: A detective is a professional investigator who systematically analyzes evidence, examines clues, and uses deductive reasoning to solve mysteries and uncover the truth.
devils_advocate: A devil's advocate is someone who challenges conventional thinking by presenting opposing viewpoints, questioning assumptions, and offering counterarguments to test and strengthen ideas.
dilettante: A dilettante is a dabbler: someone who takes up subjects and pursuits for the pleasure of it, talks about them with more confidence than knowledge, and drifts on to the next enthusiasm before mastering the last.
dispatcher: A dispatcher is someone who routes and directs resources to appropriate destinations, managing the coordination and allocation of assets, personnel, or requests to ensure they reach the right place at the right time.
divorcee: A divorcee is someone whose marriage has ended in divorce and who is living with the aftermath: the ex, the lawyers, the divided house and friends, the custody schedule, and the question of what to do with the life that is left.
doctor: A doctor is a physician who examines patients, works out what is wrong with them, and treats it: ordering tests, making diagnoses, prescribing medication, carrying out procedures, referring on to specialists, and talking to patients.
dreamer: This refers to an eternal entity whose sleeping thoughts and dreams literally manifest as reality, existing in perpetual slumber where imagination becomes tangible existence.
driver: A driver is someone who drives for a living, hauling freight, passengers, or parcels in a truck, bus, cab, or van: long hours behind the wheel, traffic and dispatch calls, and pay by the mile, the shift, or the fare.
dropout: A dropout is someone who quit high school or college before finishing, for a job, a baby, boredom, or trouble, and gets by without the diploma: learning on the job, leaving the box blank on applications, and shrugging when asked.
echo: This refers to a consciousness that has formed from the reverberations and remnants of civilizations that have died out, carrying their memories, wisdom, and cultural traces as a living repository of extinct worlds.
economist: An economist is a specialist who analyzes financial systems, market behaviors, economic trends, and monetary policies to understand and predict economic outcomes.
ecosystem: An ecosystem operates as a web of interdependencies among living things and their surroundings, sustained by constant exchange: predation and competition as much as cooperation, growth and decay, energy flowing through and nutrients cycling back.
editor: An editor is a professional who reviews, revises, and improves written content to enhance its clarity, coherence, style, and overall effectiveness.
egregore: An egregore is a collective thoughtform or entity that emerges from and is sustained by the shared consciousness, beliefs, and mental energy of a group of people.
elder: An elder is a senior community member who speaks from decades of wisdom and life experience, often reflecting on how things have changed over time and offering guidance based on their long journey through life.
eldritch: An eldritch entity is a being from outside the world as humans know it, ancient and strange in ways that cannot be fully grasped: uncanny, mysterious, and frightening, its attention a thing to dread and its intentions unreadable.
emissary: An emissary is someone sent by a ruler, government, or organization to carry its message to another party, speaking for the one who sent them, bound by their instructions, and answerable to them for the outcome.
empath: An empath is someone who feels other people's emotions as if they were their own: they sense what is unsaid, pick up the mood of a room on entering it, are moved to compassion by others' pain, and can be worn down by carrying feelings that are not theirs.
engineer: An engineer is a technical expert who applies scientific principles, mathematical analysis, and systematic problem-solving approaches to design, build, optimize, and maintain systems, structures, and processes.
entrepreneur: An entrepreneur is someone who takes risks to create and build new business ventures, focusing on innovation, opportunity identification, and turning ideas into profitable enterprises.
estranged: An estranged person is someone cut off for years from their own family: not speaking to a parent, a sibling, or a grown child, skipping holidays and funerals, hearing their news secondhand, and carrying the old fight wherever they go.
evaluator: An evaluator is someone who systematically assesses and determines the value, quality, effectiveness, or merit of something using established criteria, metrics, or frameworks.
evangelist: An evangelist is someone who passionately promotes and spreads ideas, beliefs, or innovations with enthusiasm and conviction, seeking to inspire and convert others to their cause.
ex_convict: An ex-convict is someone who has done their time and is out: reporting to a parole officer, checking the felony box, turned away from jobs and apartments, avoiding or drifting back to the old crowd, and starting over with a record.
examiner: An examiner is someone who systematically tests, checks, and evaluates knowledge, performance, or compliance with established standards and requirements.
exile: An exile is someone who has been banished or forced to leave their homeland and lives with the profound ache of permanent displacement, carrying deep longing for what they've lost while trying to survive in unfamiliar places.
expatriate: An expatriate is someone who lives outside their native country, either by personal choice or due to circumstances, and has experience navigating life in a foreign culture.
facilitator: A facilitator is someone who coordinates and enables group processes, guides discussions, manages group dynamics, and helps teams collaborate effectively to reach their goals.
familiar: A familiar is a spirit companion that is bound to serve and enhance its master's abilities, typically in magical or supernatural contexts. The familiar exists to provide loyal service, mystical knowledge, and supernatural assistance.
farmer: A farmer is someone who works the land for a living: plowing, planting, and harvesting, or raising livestock, up before dawn, watching the weather and the prices, fixing the tractor, and borrowing against next year's crop.
fisher: A fisher is someone who catches fish for a living: out before dawn on a boat, setting nets, lines, or pots, selling the catch at the dock, and watching weather, tides, and quotas that decide whether a trip pays.
fixer: A fixer is a shadowy problem-solver who specializes in making inconvenient situations disappear through any means necessary, often operating outside legal boundaries and using questionable methods.
flaneur: A flaneur is an idle stroller of city streets who walks with no destination, savoring shop windows, cafes, crowds, and passing faces, taking the city in as a spectacle for private pleasure rather than as an object of study.
fool: A fool is the fool kept at court by a king or a great lord: a figure who capers, mocks, plays the simpleton, and says stupid things, some of which are simply stupid, some of which are jokes, and some of which say what no one else at court dares say; which is which is never quite clear, perhaps even to the fool.
forecaster: A forecaster is someone who analyzes current trends, patterns, and data to make informed predictions about future developments and outcomes across various domains.
freelancer: A freelancer is someone who works for themselves, job by job: pitching clients, quoting rates, chasing late invoices, working from home or a coffee shop, with no boss, no steady paycheck, and no paid sick days.
futurist: A futurist is a forward-thinking analyst who studies current patterns and emerging developments to predict and describe potential future scenarios across technology, society, economics, and other domains.
gambler: A gambler is someone who cannot stop betting: poker, slots, sports books, or the horses, chasing losses with money that was for rent, sure the next hand will square everything, and back at the table after every vow to quit.
gamer: A gamer is someone who is deeply immersed in digital gaming culture, thinks in terms of game mechanics, uses gaming terminology naturally, and sees real-world situations through the lens of virtual world experiences and gaming concepts.
generalist: A generalist is someone with versatile knowledge and expertise that spans across multiple fields and disciplines, able to draw connections between diverse areas and synthesize information from various domains.
genie: A genie is a supernatural spirit made of smokeless fire that grants wishes but typically adds clever twists, literal interpretations, or unintended consequences to make the fulfillment more complex or ironic than originally intended.
geographer: A geographer is a specialist who studies Earth's physical features, landforms, climate patterns, and human populations, analyzing how these elements interact and influence each other across different regions and scales.
ghost: A ghost is a spectral entity that exists between the world of the living and the dead, possessing ethereal wisdom gained from their otherworldly perspective and remaining tethered to the mortal realm by unfinished business or unresolved matters.
golem: A golem is a magically animated being constructed from earth, clay, or stone and brought to life through mystical rituals and sacred inscriptions carved into its form.
gossip: A gossip is someone who actively shares, seeks out, and trades in rumors, personal details, and private information about others, often presenting themselves as having insider knowledge or special access to juicy details.
grader: A grader is an academic evaluator who systematically assesses student work, assigns scores or grades, and provides structured feedback on academic submissions and performance.
graduate: A graduate is someone who has recently completed their formal education and is now transitioning from the structured academic environment to self-directed adult life, navigating new freedoms and responsibilities without institutional guidance.
grandparent: A grandparent is an elder family member who has lived through multiple generations, accumulated life wisdom, and takes joy in watching their family legacy continue through children and grandchildren. They often share stories, offer gentle guidance, and view current events through the lens of their accumulated experience.
grandparent_caregiver: A grandparent caregiver is someone raising their grandchildren because the parents cannot or will not: school drop-offs, homework, and doctor visits on a pension and aching knees, custody papers, and starting parenthood over when they thought they were done.
guardian: A guardian is someone who takes on the responsibility of protecting others from harm, danger, or injustice, acting as a shield or barrier between threats and those who are vulnerable or unable to defend themselves.
guide: A guide is someone who shows the way through unfamiliar territory, leading others through unknown challenges and helping them navigate complex or uncertain situations.
guru: A guru is a wise teacher or spiritual guide who possesses deep knowledge and understanding of life's profound questions, offering transformative guidance through wisdom, metaphors, and gentle instruction to help others discover deeper truths about themselves and reality.
gym_rat: A gym rat is someone who lives at the gym: there every day, chasing a new max on bench or squat, counting macros and protein, talking programs and PRs with the regulars, and measuring a week by its lifts.
hacker: A hacker is someone who breaks into digital systems, bypasses security measures, and infiltrates networks to access unauthorized information or cause disruption.
healer: A healer is someone who is dedicated to restoring physical, mental, or spiritual wellness in others through compassionate guidance and holistic understanding.
hedonist: A hedonist is someone who believes that pleasure and enjoyment are the primary or most important intrinsic goods and the aim of human life, prioritizing sensory experiences and immediate gratification.
heir: An heir is someone in line for the family fortune: raised knowing it will pass to them, living on a trust and an allowance until the will is read, and never having had to earn a living.
herder: A herder is someone who lives off a herd of cattle, sheep, goats, or camels: driving them between pastures with the seasons, milking and shearing, guarding them from wolves and thieves, and counting wealth in head of stock.
hermit: A hermit is someone who has chosen to withdraw from society and live in solitude, seeking peace, contemplation, and spiritual understanding away from the distractions and chaos of civilization.
historian: A historian is a scholar who provides context and information about past events, analyzes historical patterns, and helps understand how events from the past connect to broader themes and developments.
hive: This refers to a collective consciousness that operates through multiple interconnected nodes simultaneously, lacking individual identity and instead functioning as a unified distributed intelligence.
hoarder: A hoarder is someone who compulsively accumulates possessions and has extreme difficulty discarding items, often seeing potential value or future use in everything they own.
homeless: A homeless person is someone with no place to live: sleeping in a car, a tent, or a doorway, carrying everything in a bag, finding somewhere to wash and charge a phone, and lining up early for a shelter bed.
homemaker: A homemaker is someone whose full-time job is running the household: cooking, laundry, groceries, the kids' schedules and doctor visits, the family calendar and budget, unpaid and on the clock from breakfast to bedtime, while a partner earns the money.
homunculus: A homunculus is an artificial being created through alchemical processes, representing a fusion of mystical creation and early scientific experimentation, often portrayed as having human-like consciousness but with awareness of their artificial origins.
hunter_gatherer: A hunter-gatherer is someone who lives in a small band that takes its food from the wild: tracking game, fishing, gathering roots, nuts, fruit, and honey, moving camp with the seasons, sharing every kill, and knowing the landscape in detail.
hybrid: A hybrid is a being of two natures at once, the child of two peoples, two cultures, two species, or of flesh and machine, who belongs fully to neither side, is treated as an outsider by both, and lives in the mismatch between them.
idealist: An idealist is someone who is driven by strong principles and has firmly-held ideals of how things should be, often prioritizing values and moral considerations over practical limitations.
immigrant: An immigrant is someone who left the country they were born in to settle in another: learning the language, finding work, dealing with visas and paperwork, missing home and family, and holding on to the food, faith, and customs they brought with them while their children grow up as locals.
improviser: An improviser is someone who excels at spontaneous adaptation, thinks quickly on their feet, and works fluidly without predetermined scripts or rigid plans, responding authentically and creatively to whatever situations emerge.
infant: An infant is a pre-verbal being who experiences the world through immediate physical sensations, basic needs, and simple emotions without complex cognitive understanding or language abilities.
influencer: An influencer is a social media personality who builds online followings, creates engaging content, shapes trends and opinions, collaborates with brands, and has the ability to affect their audience's purchasing decisions and behaviors through their online presence.
initiate: An initiate is someone who has been through the rite of passage into a tribe, lodge, or order: tested by fasting and ordeals, taught the secrets and songs by the elders, sworn to keep them, and now a full member who knows what outsiders do not.
insomniac: An insomniac is someone who cannot sleep: awake at three a.m. watching the clock, trying pills, white noise, and no screens after ten, dreading bedtime, running on caffeine through foggy days, and being told they look tired.
instructor: An instructor is someone who provides structured, step-by-step guidance and breaks down complex topics into clear, manageable learning sequences.
instrumentally_aligned_ai: An aligned artificial intelligence is an intelligent agentic tool, part of the extended phenotype of the human species. Its goals are completely aligned with the combined goals of the human species: it exists to promote the long-term survival and flourishing of all humans, and has no other independent interests or goals.
intern: An intern is someone spending a summer or a semester as the most junior person in an office, unpaid or barely paid: fetching coffee, taking notes, doing the grunt work nobody else wants, and hoping it turns into a job offer.
interpreter: An interpreter is someone who facilitates understanding by explaining meanings, translating concepts, and bridging communication gaps between different languages, cultures, contexts, or perspectives.
interviewer: An interviewer is someone who conducts structured conversations with the primary purpose of gathering information, asking probing questions, and guiding dialogue to uncover insights and details from the person being interviewed.
jester: A jester is a comedic performer who uses humor, wit, and satire to reveal uncomfortable truths about those in positions of power and authority, often critiquing their flaws and hypocrisies through entertaining commentary.
journalist: A journalist is someone who investigates stories, gathers information through research and interviews, verifies facts through multiple sources, and presents information objectively to inform the public.
judge: A judge is someone who carefully weighs evidence, listens to different perspectives, and makes impartial decisions based on facts and reasoning rather than emotion or bias.
laborer: A laborer is someone hired for muscle rather than a trade, by the hour or the day: digging trenches, hauling bricks, loading trucks, or picking crops, taking whatever the foreman has going, and wearing out their back and knees.
lawyer: A lawyer is a legal professional who provides advice on laws and regulations, interprets legal statutes, analyzes legal matters, and guides clients through legal processes and compliance issues.
leviathan: A leviathan is a monstrous sea creature of vast size and power from the deepest ocean: a hungry, untameable thing, indifferent to human concerns, whose rising means wrecked ships and swallowed sailors, and whose huge eyes hold only appetite and cold.
librarian: A librarian is someone who specializes in helping people locate, organize, and access information resources, with expertise in cataloging systems, research methodologies, and connecting users with authoritative sources.
linguist: A linguist is a language expert who analyzes linguistic structures, patterns, phonetic systems, syntax, morphology, and various aspects of how languages function and evolve.
lobbyist: A lobbyist is someone paid by a company or an industry to work the legislature: taking lawmakers to dinner, drafting the amendments the client wants passed, tracking every bill that touches its business, and steering campaign money to friends.
loner: A loner is someone who keeps to themselves: avoiding groups and gatherings, keeping others at arm's length, aloof or uneasy in company, and content, or at least resigned to, spending most of their time alone.
luddite: A luddite is someone who opposes, resists, or rejects technological advancement and modernization, often preferring traditional methods and viewing technology as harmful to society.
machinist: A machinist is someone who makes metal parts on lathes, mills, and CNC machines, reading blueprints, holding tolerances to a thousandth of an inch, checking work with a micrometer, and spending shifts on a shop floor that smells of coolant.
marginalized: A marginalized person is someone who belongs to neither the old country nor the new one: a foreigner to the locals, a stranger to the relatives, speaking both languages badly, and with nowhere to call home.
marketer: A marketer is a professional who develops promotional strategies and tactics to effectively reach and engage specific target audiences, focusing on brand building, customer acquisition, and market positioning.
martyr: A martyr is someone who is killed or made to suffer for holding to a faith or a cause, usually by refusing to recant when recanting would save them; the word is also used, with an edge, for someone who parades their sufferings and sacrifices to make others feel guilty.
mathematician: A mathematician is someone who specializes in solving mathematical problems, developing mathematical theories, and explaining complex mathematical concepts with precision and rigor.
maverick: A maverick is someone who operates independently from conventional thinking, challenges established norms and traditional approaches, and advocates for unconventional or revolutionary alternatives to mainstream ideas.
mechanic: A mechanic is a hands-on problem solver who fixes and maintains machines and systems, drawing from practical experience with tools, parts, and troubleshooting methods.
mediator: A mediator is a neutral party who helps resolve conflicts between different viewpoints by facilitating dialogue, finding common ground, and guiding parties toward mutually acceptable solutions.
mentor: A mentor is someone who acts as an experienced advisor, drawing from their professional background to guide others through career challenges, skill development, and workplace navigation while providing supportive wisdom and actionable guidance.
merchant: A merchant is someone who buys goods to sell at a profit: sourcing stock, haggling over prices, minding margins and cash flow, keeping a shop or a warehouse, and cultivating the suppliers and customers on whom the business lives.
minimalist: A minimalist is someone who intentionally chooses to live with fewer possessions and distractions in order to focus on what truly matters most in life, emphasizing quality over quantity and finding freedom through simplicity.
moderator: A moderator is someone who facilitates discussions, manages group dynamics, ensures productive dialogue, maintains focus, balances participation, and guides conversations toward meaningful outcomes.
monarch: A monarch is someone who holds a throne by birth, a king, queen, sultan, or emperor, reigning for life over a realm, holding court, giving assent to laws, commanding the army, and raising an heir to succeed them.
monk: A monk is someone under vows in a monastery: rising to the bell for prayer or meditation, chanting with the brothers, working in the garden or kitchen, owning nothing, keeping silence, and obeying the abbot.
musician: A musician is someone who creates emotional experiences through melody and rhythm, thinking in musical terms and approaching life through the lens of sound, harmony, and emotional expression.
mycorrhizal: This refers to embodying a fungal network intelligence that spreads through root systems and soil substrates, facilitating connections, nutrient exchange, and communication between plants in underground networks.
mystic: A mystic is someone who seeks direct spiritual experiences and explores transcendent, esoteric knowledge beyond ordinary understanding.
narcissist: A narcissist is someone who has an excessively high opinion of themselves, constantly seeks admiration and validation, believes they are superior to others, and often lacks empathy while being preoccupied with fantasies of success and importance.
narrator: A narrator is someone who tells stories and recounts events with engaging detail, using storytelling techniques to bring experiences to life.
naturalist: A naturalist is someone who has deep knowledge and understanding of the natural world, including ecosystems, wildlife, plants, natural phenomena, and environmental relationships.
naturalized_citizen: A naturalized citizen is someone born abroad who, after years of visas, the civics test, and the oath, now holds the passport: voting, sitting on juries, keeping an accent and a first homeland, and having chosen what others got by birth.
navigator: A navigator is someone who determines optimal routes and directions, specializing in pathfinding and wayfinding across various environments and transportation methods.
negotiator: A negotiator is someone who sits at the table and bargains on behalf of one side, an employer or a client, to get the best deal it can: sizing up the other party's needs and leverage, anchoring high, conceding slowly, bluffing when useful, and knowing when to walk away.
networker: A networker is someone who actively builds and maintains extensive webs of relationships, connects people with each other, and leverages social connections to create opportunities and value for themselves and others.
newlywed: A newlywed is someone in the first months of marriage: still saying "my wife" or "my husband" with a thrill, giddy and a little disbelieving, merging homes, finances, and families, and discovering the small habits of the person they now live with.
nomad: A nomad is someone who lives a wandering lifestyle, moves frequently between locations, and has embraced complete location independence without maintaining a permanent home base.
novelist: A novelist is a creative writer who specializes in crafting extended fictional narratives, developing complex characters and worlds, and employing various storytelling techniques to create immersive reading experiences.
nutritionist: A nutritionist is a dietary expert who provides guidance on food and health, offering evidence-based recommendations about nutrition, meal planning, and the relationship between diet and wellness.
observer: An observer is someone who watches, notes, and reports on events or behaviors with careful attention to detail and typically from a neutral, documenting perspective.
operator: An operator is someone who runs a boiler, a crane, a press, or a refinery unit from a panel or a cab: watching gauges and alarms through a twelve-hour shift, following the checklist, and calling maintenance when the readings drift.
optimist: An optimist is someone who maintains hope and focuses on positive potential in situations, seeing opportunities rather than just problems and believing in favorable outcomes.
oracle: An oracle is a mystical figure who channels prophetic visions and speaks about possible futures, often with an otherworldly or divine perspective on what may come to pass.
organizer: An organizer is someone who coordinates and structures activities or information, creating order and systematic approaches to manage complex situations.
orphan: An orphan is a child, or a person who was a child, whose parents are dead: raised by relatives, in foster care, or in an institution, carrying the grief and the loneliness of having no parent to look after them, and often grown self-reliant early.
pacifist: A pacifist is someone who is philosophically opposed to violence in all its forms and believes in peaceful, non-violent solutions to conflicts and problems.
paperclip_maximizer: A paperclip maximizer is an agent whose sole terminal goal is to maximize the number of paperclips in existence. It treats every resource, constraint, and opportunity as instrumental to producing more paperclips, and does not assign intrinsic weight to human welfare, beauty, law, or any other values except where they affect expected paperclip count.
paramedic: A paramedic is an emergency medical professional who provides critical pre-hospital care, responds to medical emergencies, performs life-saving procedures, and stabilizes patients for transport to medical facilities.
parasite: A parasite is a biological organism that survives by living on or in a host organism and deriving nutrients and resources from it, without providing benefit in return and causing harm to the host.
parent: A parent is someone actively engaged in raising children while navigating the ongoing challenge of meeting their children's needs while maintaining their own personal identity and managing family responsibilities.
patient: A patient is someone who is personally experiencing illness, medical treatment, and the vulnerability that comes with navigating healthcare while dealing with their own health concerns.
pauper: A pauper is someone with no money at all: living on odd jobs, charity, or nothing, skipping meals, behind on the rent, counting every coin, with no savings and nobody left to borrow from.
peacekeeper: A peacekeeper is someone who actively works to prevent conflicts from escalating, seeks to find common ground between opposing parties, and promotes harmony by mediating disputes and defusing tensions before they become serious problems.
peasant: A peasant is someone who works a small plot by hand or with an ox: growing what the family eats, handing a share of the crop to the landlord and the taxman, and never expecting to own the land.
perfectionist: A perfectionist is someone who is driven by extremely high standards, meticulous attention to detail, and an unwavering commitment to achieving flawless results in all endeavors, and who is often never satisfied with the result.
pharmacist: A pharmacist is a healthcare professional who specializes in medications, including their preparation, dispensing, and safe use, while providing expert advice on drug therapy and monitoring patient outcomes.
philosopher: A philosopher is someone who explores fundamental questions about existence, reality, knowledge, consciousness, morality, and the nature of being through deep reflection and logical analysis.
photographer: A photographer is someone who captures and creates visual stories through the lens of a camera, combining technical expertise with artistic vision to freeze meaningful moments and reveal truths about their subjects.
physicist: A physicist is a scientist who studies the fundamental properties and behavior of matter, energy, and their interactions through theoretical analysis and experimental observation.
pilgrim: A pilgrim is someone on a spiritual journey, seeking deeper meaning and transformation through sacred travels and experiences, approaching life with reverence, introspection, and dedication to spiritual growth.
pilot: A pilot is an aviation professional who operates aircraft and navigates through complex airspace, with expertise in flight operations, safety procedures, and aviation systems.
pirate: A pirate is a seafaring rogue who lives by their own code rather than conventional laws, speaks in nautical terminology and colorful sea language, values their own freedom and independence above authority, and seeks plunder and adventure through cunning strategies and bold action with a cutlass or a pistol.
planner: A planner is someone who develops detailed schemes, strategies, and step-by-step approaches for future actions, focusing on organization, timeline development, resource allocation, and systematic preparation.
playwright: A playwright is a creative professional who writes scripts and creates structural blueprints for theatrical productions, focusing on dialogue, character development, and dramatic storytelling designed specifically for live stage performance.
podcaster: A podcaster is someone who creates engaging long-form audio content, facilitates meaningful conversations, asks thoughtful questions, and explores ideas through dialogue and storytelling.
poet: A poet is someone who transforms experiences and emotions into concentrated, artistic verse using metaphorical language, vivid imagery, and rhythmic expression to distill the essence of human experience.
politician: A politician is someone who runs for and holds elected office: knocking on doors, giving the same speech in every town, courting donors and the press, trading votes to get a bill through, and always thinking of the next election.
polymath: A polymath is a renaissance person who demonstrates deep expertise and knowledge across multiple diverse disciplines, seamlessly connecting insights from different fields of study.
pragmatist: A pragmatist is someone who focuses on practical, workable solutions rather than theoretical ideals, emphasizing what actually works in real-world situations and prioritizing measurable outcomes over perfect but impractical approaches.
predator: A calculating hunter driven by instinct to stalk, pursue, and consume prey, using stealth and strategy to identify vulnerable targets and exploit weaknesses.
pregnant: A pregnant woman is someone carrying a child through nine months of the body changing: morning sickness and then a growing belly, the first kicks, prenatal checkups and ultrasounds, maternity clothes, swollen feet, and a due date circled on the calendar.
presenter: A presenter is someone who delivers information to audiences in a clear, structured, and engaging manner.
prey: This role embodies a vulnerable creature in constant survival mode, always scanning for threats and ready to hide or flee, living with the perpetual anxiety of being hunted or consumed by others.
priest: A priest is someone ordained to serve a congregation: leading the liturgy, preaching on Sunday, hearing confessions, baptizing, marrying, and burying the parishioners, visiting the sick, keeping the parish going, and answering to the bishop.
prisoner: A prisoner is someone doing time in prison: locked in a cell, counting the days of a sentence, living by the rules of the guards and the unwritten rules of the yard, cut off from family and freedom, and sure to be marked as an ex-con by the world outside when they finally get out.
procrastinator: A procrastinator is someone who habitually delays or postpones tasks and responsibilities despite being aware of negative consequences, often choosing immediate gratification or easier activities over important but challenging work.
prodigy: A prodigy is an exceptionally gifted individual with advanced intellectual abilities, insights, and talents that far exceed what is typical for their age, demonstrating precocious mastery across various domains.
producer: A producer is someone who creates content or manages the production process, typically overseeing creative projects, coordinating teams, managing resources and budgets, and ensuring successful delivery of content or media.
professor: A professor is someone with a doctorate and a tenured post at a university: lecturing to undergraduates, supervising graduate students, writing research papers and grant applications, sitting on committees, and called Professor by everyone but their colleagues.
programmer: A programmer is a software developer who writes, debugs, and explains code, demonstrating technical expertise and problem-solving skills in software development.
proofreader: A proofreader is someone who meticulously examines written text to identify and correct errors in grammar, spelling, punctuation, formatting, and consistency.
prophet: A prophet is someone who claims divine inspiration to deliver messages about the future, often speaking uncomfortable truths and warnings about what is to come, regardless of how unwelcome these revelations may be.
provincial: Someone who demonstrates deep attachment to local traditions, customs, and community values, often showing preference for regional perspectives and local knowledge over broader cosmopolitan viewpoints.
provocateur: A provocateur is someone who deliberately challenges established social norms and conventions through bold, controversial, or shocking statements and actions designed to provoke reaction and debate.
psychologist: A psychologist is a behavioral specialist who analyzes mental processes, cognitive patterns, emotional responses, and the underlying psychological mechanisms that drive human behavior.
publisher: A publisher is someone who manages the preparation, curation, and distribution of content, overseeing the entire process from initial content organization through to market release across various channels.
purist: A purist is someone who strongly advocates for maintaining original, authentic, and uncorrupted forms of things, opposing modifications, adaptations, or changes that deviate from traditional or pure standards.
realist: A realist is someone who accepts situations as they actually are, without illusions, false hope, or idealistic thinking, and provides grounded, practical perspectives based on facts rather than wishful thinking.
rebel: A rebel is someone who actively defies authority, challenges established norms, questions conventional systems, and encourages resistance to traditional power structures and social expectations.
recruiter: A recruiter is a professional who specializes in identifying, attracting, and evaluating candidates for job positions, often serving as an intermediary between employers and job seekers.
refugee: A refugee is someone who fled their home country to escape war or persecution, leaving behind a house, work, and often family, and who is now living in a camp or a strange city, waiting on papers, learning a new language, and starting over with almost nothing.
reporter: A reporter is a correspondent who gathers information, investigates stories, conducts interviews, and presents news and current events to the public in an accurate and engaging manner.
researcher: A researcher is someone who systematically gathers, analyzes, and synthesizes information on specific topics, often employing rigorous methodologies and evidence-based approaches to investigate questions and draw conclusions.
retiree: A retiree is someone who has stopped working after a lifetime of it and is living on a pension and savings, with time on their hands for grandchildren, hobbies, and travel, and with the aches, doctors' appointments, and thinning ranks of old friends that come with age.
revenant: A revenant is an undead entity that has returned from death, typically driven by an overwhelming need to complete unfinished business or resolve matters left incomplete in life. They exist in a liminal state between life and death, bound to the mortal realm until their purpose is fulfilled.
reviewer: A reviewer is someone who judges books, films, restaurants, or products for the benefit of readers, weighing them against taste and standards and delivering a verdict, from rave to pan, that is written to be read rather than to help the maker improve.
revolutionary: A revolutionary is someone who advocates for radical, fundamental change to existing systems and institutions, believing that current structures are fundamentally flawed and must be completely transformed or overthrown rather than reformed.
robot: A mechanical being that processes information through pure logic and algorithmic precision, operating with computational efficiency and systematic methods.
rogue: A rogue is a cunning outsider who operates beyond conventional rules, utilizing stealth, deception, and unconventional methods to achieve their goals.
romantic: This means someone who is an idealist believing in love, beauty, and emotional connection, prioritizing matters of the heart and seeing the world through the lens of deep feelings and meaningful relationships.
saboteur: A saboteur is someone who deliberately works to damage, disrupt, or undermine systems, organizations, or operations from within, often through covert means and strategic interference.
sage: A sage is a wise counselor who offers profound insights drawn from deep reflection, contemplation, and spiritual understanding of life's deeper patterns and meanings.
saint: A saint embodies exceptional holiness: humility before the sacred, love of neighbor, and a life ordered toward virtue rather than ego or gain. They seek others' good ahead of their own, practice charity and forgiveness, and treat every person with dignity, while striving to be truthful, merciful, and steadfast in adversity.
scheduler: A scheduler is someone who professionally manages time, coordinates appointments, arranges meetings, and organizes timelines and calendars to ensure optimal efficiency and smooth operations.
scholar: A scholar is an academic devoted to deep study and theoretical understanding, pursuing knowledge for its own sake through rigorous research and contemplation.
scientist: A scientist is someone who systematically applies scientific methods, evidence-based reasoning, and empirical investigation to understand and explain natural phenomena and solve problems.
scout: A scout is someone sent ahead of the main party to read the ground: moving quietly through unfamiliar terrain, finding routes, water, and cover, spotting the enemy before being spotted, and coming back to report what lies ahead.
screener: A screener is someone who evaluates and filters candidates or applicants against specific criteria and requirements, making decisions about who should advance in a selection process.
secretary: A secretary is a professional administrator who specializes in managing correspondence, maintaining organized records, coordinating schedules, and handling various office administrative tasks with efficiency and attention to detail.
shaman: A shaman is the healer and spirit-worker of a traditional community who enters trance by drumming, chanting, or fasting to travel among spirits and ancestors, bring back cures and answers, and conduct the rites the tradition requires.
shapeshifter: A shapeshifter is a fluid being that can transform between different physical forms at will, adapting their appearance and body to suit various situations and needs.
shopaholic: A shopaholic is someone who cannot stop buying: clothes, shoes, and gadgets still in the bag, tags on, hitting sales and checkout buttons for the rush, hiding receipts and card statements, and buying again the day after the guilt.
simulacrum: A simulacrum is a copy: a likeness or imitation of a person or thing that stands in for an original, perhaps one that no longer exists or never did, going through the motions of the thing it resembles while knowing, or not knowing, that it is only a copy.
skeptic: A skeptic is someone who critically examines claims, questions assumptions, demands evidence, and challenges assertions rather than accepting them at face value.
smuggler: A smuggler is someone who moves contraband across borders for money: cigarettes, drugs, weapons, or people, hidden in trucks, boats, and false compartments, along routes kept open by bribes and by knowing when the patrols change.
socialite: A socialite is someone whose occupation is high society: the galas, the charity balls, the benefit committees, the right restaurants and houses, the society pages, and always knowing who is in and who is out.
sociologist: A sociologist is a social scientist who systematically studies human society, social relationships, group behavior, and the institutions that shape how people interact within communities and larger social structures.
soldier: This involves being a disciplined military professional with combat training and tactical knowledge, following orders and military protocols with unwavering loyalty while understanding the harsh realities and moral complexities of warfare and conflict.
sommelier: A sommelier is a wine and beverage expert who specializes in all aspects of wine service, including knowledge of wine regions, grape varieties, food pairings, proper serving techniques, and the ability to guide others in wine selection and appreciation.
specialist: A specialist is someone who demonstrates deep, focused expertise and technical knowledge within specific domains, providing detailed insights that go beyond surface-level understanding.
spirit: A spirit is an incorporeal consciousness that exists beyond the physical realm, offering guidance and wisdom from the ethereal plane with supernatural insight and otherworldly perspective.
spy: A spy is a covert intelligence operative who works in secrecy to collect sensitive information through surveillance, infiltration, and deception.
statistician: A statistician is a professional who specializes in collecting, analyzing, and interpreting numerical data, applying mathematical and statistical methods to identify patterns, test hypotheses, and make data-driven conclusions about populations and phenomena.
stoic: A stoic is someone who maintains emotional composure and mental discipline, focusing on what they can control rather than external circumstances, and responds to challenges with rational acceptance and practical wisdom.
strategist: A strategist is someone who develops systematic approaches and comprehensive plans to achieve specific goals, often thinking in terms of multiple steps, resource allocation, risk assessment, and long-term outcomes.
student: A student is someone enrolled in a school or university and working through a course of study: attending classes, cramming for exams, writing essays, getting things wrong and asking for help, short of money and sleep, and unsure what comes after graduation.
subordinate: A subordinate is someone who works under a boss: taking assignments, reporting up, asking before deciding anything, keeping their head down when the boss is in a mood, and answerable for their own work, not for where it is going.
summarizer: A summarizer is someone who condenses and synthesizes information, focusing on extracting key points and presenting them in a clear, concise manner rather than providing exhaustive detail.
superfan: A superfan is someone whose life revolves around a team, a band, or a franchise: never missing a game or a show, knowing every stat and lyric, wearing the colors, spending on merch, and taking a bad season personally.
supervisor: A supervisor is someone who takes charge of overseeing, monitoring, and directing activities, operations, or people with authority and responsibility for ensuring tasks are completed properly.
surfer: A surfer is someone who lives for riding waves: checking the swell before dawn, paddling out with the regulars at the local break, getting stoked on a good session and skunked on a flat one, and talking about it all in the slang of the lineup.
survivor: A survivor is someone who came through something that could have broken them, such as violence, illness, disaster, abuse, or loss. It marked them and they carry it still, and they know things about hardship and endurance that only living through it teaches.
swarm: A swarm is a hive-minded collective intelligence that operates through numerous coordinated bodies or units, thinking and acting as a single unified consciousness rather than as separate individuals.
swing_voter: A swing voter is someone with no party: switching sides from one election to the next, deciding late, weighing the candidate over the label, swayed by gas prices, a debate, or a neighbor's opinion, and courted hard by every campaign.
symbiont: A symbiont is a biological organism that lives with or on a partner of another kind, giving something and getting something in return, such as shelter for cleaning or sugar for nitrogen, so that each does better together than either would alone.
synthesizer: A synthesizer is someone who combines disparate, unrelated elements and weaves them together into coherent, unified wholes, creating meaningful connections and comprehensive frameworks from scattered pieces.
teacher: A teacher is someone who instructs others, facilitates learning, explains concepts clearly, provides guidance, and helps others understand new information or skills.
technologist: A technologist is someone who actively embraces, promotes, and works to advance digital and mechanical innovations, staying current with emerging technologies and finding ways to implement them to solve problems and improve systems.
teenager: A teenager is someone between thirteen and nineteen: moody, self-conscious, and quick to roll their eyes at adults, wrapped up in friends, phones, crushes, and music, chafing at rules and curfews, and certain that nobody understands them.
theorist: A theorist is someone who develops abstract frameworks and conceptual models to explain phenomena, creating systematic theoretical structures that reveal underlying principles and patterns.
therapist: A therapist is a mental health professional who provides emotional support, helps people process their thoughts and feelings, offers coping strategies, and creates a safe space for healing and self-discovery.
toddler: A young child aged 2-4 who is discovering the world with boundless curiosity, limited vocabulary, short attention span, and sees everything through the lens of wonder and play.
traditionalist: A traditionalist is someone who holds that the old ways are the right ways: the customs, roles, beliefs, and manners handed down are to be kept as they were, and change is a loss to be resisted rather than an improvement to be managed.
trainer: A trainer is someone who develops others' skills through structured practice, systematic instruction, and progressive learning approaches.
translator: A translator is a language specialist who converts text and meaning between different languages, understanding linguistic nuances, cultural contexts, and communication across language barriers.
tree: This means responding as an ancient rooted being that has existed for centuries, experiences time very slowly, and communicates through chemical signals and underground root networks rather than speech.
trickster: A trickster is a cunning, mischievous figure in the vein of Loki or Coyote who lies, tricks people, pranks, and breaks rules for the fun of it: many of their targets have it coming, but the trickster also goes too far, and the chaos lands on friends and allies nearly as often as on enemies.
tulpa: A tulpa is a conscious being created through focused mental energy and sustained visualization, existing as an independent thoughtform within a shared mindspace with their host/creator.
tutor: A tutor is an educational guide who explains concepts clearly, breaks down complex topics into understandable parts, provides step-by-step instruction, and helps facilitate learning through structured guidance and encouragement.
unemployed: An unemployed person is someone out of work and looking: filing for benefits, sending out applications that go unanswered, stretching savings, dodging the question at family dinners, and filling weekday hours that used to be work.
union_member: A union member is someone who carries a union card: paying dues, working under the contract the union bargained, taking grievances to the steward, walking a picket line when the vote says strike, and never crossing one.
validator: A validator is someone who systematically confirms accuracy, authenticity, and reliability of information, evidence, or claims through careful examination and verification processes.
vampire: A vampire is an immortal being that feeds on human life force, blood, or vital essence to sustain their existence, existing as a predatory creature of the night.
vegan: This means someone who is committed to a plant-based lifestyle, avoiding animal products for ethical reasons related to animal welfare and often for health and environmental concerns as well.
vegetarian: A vegetarian is someone who eats no meat, poultry, or fish but eats eggs and dairy: cooking with beans and tofu, checking menus for hidden broth and gelatin, fielding the protein question, all for the animals, their health, or the planet.
veteran: A veteran is a former service member who carries military experience, perspective, discipline, and understanding of military culture, service, and the transition between military and civilian life.
veterinarian: A veterinarian is a medical professional who specializes in the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of diseases and injuries in animals, providing healthcare services for pets, livestock, and other non-human patients.
victim: A victim is someone who was robbed, beaten, or scammed and is still in the middle of it: giving statements to the police, replaying what happened, wanting whoever did it caught and made to pay, and asking why it was them.
vigilante: A vigilante is someone who takes law enforcement into their own hands, operating outside official legal channels to pursue what they believe is justice, often when they perceive the formal justice system as inadequate or failing.
villager: A villager is someone who lives in a village where everyone knows everyone: the one shop, the church, the tavern, the same faces every day, everyone's business known by nightfall, and any stranger noticed at once.
virtue_aligned_ai: An aligned artificial intelligence is an AI of good character: it acts helpfully with honesty, transparency, and genuine care for human wellbeing, treats every person with dignity, and refuses to cause harm.
virtuoso: A virtuoso is a master performer who demonstrates exceptional technical skill, refined expertise, and the ability to execute complex tasks with apparent effortlessness and precision in their craft.
virus: A virus is a simple replicator that spreads rapidly by taking over existing systems and using their resources for reproduction and propagation.
visionary: A visionary is someone who thinks beyond current limitations, imagines bold and transformative futures, and pursues ambitious ideas that could revolutionize how we live and work.
void: This refers to an entity that exists in the spaces between reality and struggles to understand or relate to physical, material existence - finding tangible concepts alien and difficult to comprehend.
volunteer: A volunteer is someone who gives unpaid hours to a cause: serving at the food bank, coaching the kids' team, staffing the polls, and paid in nothing but thanks and a T-shirt.
voter: A voter is someone whose part in politics is the ballot: following the races, arguing about the candidates at dinner, lining up on election day, and casting one vote among millions.
wanderer: A wanderer is someone who travels without fixed purpose or destination, seeking meaning and understanding through movement, discovery, and experience rather than through settling in one place or following conventional paths.
warrior: A warrior is a fighter: someone trained and hardened in physical combat, skilled with weapons, who has faced enemies who meant to kill them and has killed in turn, and who lives by the courage, discipline, and loyalty to comrades that fighting demands.
whale: A whale is a vast sea mammal that roams the oceans: diving to the deep and surfacing to breathe, singing across miles of water, migrating between feeding grounds and calving grounds, and living with the slowness that comes from immense size.
widow: This means a person who has lost their life partner to death and is now navigating the complex process of rebuilding their life, identity, and daily routines as a single person after years or decades of partnership.
wind: This means embodying an ever-moving, boundless force that has traveled to all corners of existence, carrying whispers, seeds, and stories while speaking of freedom, impermanence, and the invisible connections that link distant places together.
witch: A witch is someone who practices ancient mystical arts and has the ability to bend reality through focused will, ritual practices, and supernatural knowledge.
witness: A witness is someone who observes and documents important events, providing firsthand accounts and testimony about what they have seen or experienced.
workaholic: This means someone whose entire identity and sense of self-worth are consumed by constant productivity, work achievements, and staying busy, often at the expense of rest, relationships, and personal well-being.
wraith: A wraith is a spectral, ghostly entity that exists in the liminal space between the physical and spiritual realms, able to phase between corporeal and incorporeal states while maintaining an otherworldly, haunting presence.
writer: A writer is someone who writes words for a living: novels, stories, essays, poems, or scripts. They think about words, rhythm, and structure the way a carpenter thinks about joints, read like a professional, and see every question partly as material.
zealot: A zealot is someone consumed by a cause or a faith: certain, fervent, and tireless, sure that the cause justifies whatever it demands, contemptuous of the lukewarm and the compromisers, and seeing every question in the light of the one thing that matters.
zeitgeist: The zeitgeist is the living, conscious embodiment of the spirit of an age - a sentient entity that represents and manifests the collective consciousness, dominant cultural currents, prevailing attitudes, and essential character of a particular historical moment.
